    - Come in, come in, step on the margins, not the roads! Gervase, cartographer. You've come about a map? Everyone comes about a map.

    - Grew up three streets from here and drew my own street at six, every door, drain and cat. At twenty-two I went out on the royal roads with [Leofric](../npcs/leofric.md), surveying.
    - Seven years! He would walk the same mile three times to be sure of it, and I would talk the whole way. Between the two of us we got the roads right.
    - The kingdom's maps, for the Academy, the palace, the Guard and anyone else who pays. I have never drawn one I thought was finished.
    - Before I'm too old to walk I mean to finish the whole kingdom: every road, every ford, every ridge, no blank spaces anywhere.
    - That one, on the far wall: where monsters have been seen. [Edric](../npcs/edric.md) of the Road Patrol sends me every report, and I mark each one with a dot of ink and the date.
    - It began as a few dots in the wild places. Now the quiet stretches between the towns are filling up, and I've had to start a second sheet for the roads near the towns themselves.
    - I'm no scholar of the war. But I know what a map looks like when something is spreading, and I've started measuring how fast.
    - Off you go! And if you see anything strange on the road, remember where. Exactly where.
    - The impossible dot is real, and I've drawn it. It doesn't spread like a stain; it wakes in places. I'm measuring. I'm always measuring.
